label: Red Clay Flats, symptom 'drive_grease_degradation'
headline: Red Clay Flats' 10x tracker-grease rate is an artifact of booking routine regreases as corrective work orders while other sites book identical jobs as PMs - no defect, no reported production loss, and the underlying wear is vintage-driven.
action: Fix the work-order coding by folding tracker-drive lubrication PMs into the same numerator/denominator as CM grease work, then re-run the site-symptom rate before any field action; separately hand the technicians' block-sweep regrease suggestion to the site PM planner.
reasoning: The controls contain the same phenomenon, described in near-verbatim language, but coded as PM rather than CM: WO-2024-00406 (Tallow Branch, PM) is almost word-for-word identical to cluster members WO-2026-00664 and WO-2026-00688, and WO-2024-00308 is a Red Clay Flats PM with the identical 'third one in this block this quarter... normal wear for the vintage' text that was not counted in this CM-based cluster. WO-2026-00052 (Ashvale Dry Lake) repeats the 'dried out and gritty' narrative of WO-2025-01242 at another site, and Dry Creek/Caprock/Cypress controls show the same lubrication touches booked as 'routine_service' PMs — so the fleet denominator is systematically capturing this work outside the CM channel, which is exactly what H3 predicts. H1 is also well supported by the member text itself ('same vintage', 'all coming up to that age together', 'normal wear for the vintage' in WO-2024-00054, WO-2024-00064, WO-2025-00728, WO-2026-00664), so the underlying events look like an age-cohort regrease need rather than a defect; H2 fails because no member cites clay dust or an external site-local trigger (all environment fields are 'none_mentioned') and no other tribology symptom at the site is shown to be elevated. H4 is partially consistent (events arrive in same-week pairs 2024-07-26/29, 2025-12-06/22, 2026-06-24/28), further shrinking the effective independent event count. With zero reported production loss, P2/P3 priorities and 2.0-6.9 labor hours per event, the 10x lift is best read as a CM/PM coding difference over ordinary vintage wear, not a systemic finding.
contradicting: Two members were not simple regreases: WO-2025-00728 and WO-2025-01195 record drive replacements with gear faces scored from running dry, which is real hardware consumption rather than a coding nuance. The Red Clay Flats PM control WO-2024-00308 also shows lubrication touches at this site beyond the seven CM records, so the site's total lubrication burden may genuinely exceed peers even if the CM-only rate overstates it. Technicians in WO-2026-00664 and WO-2026-00688 explicitly recommend a block/zone-wide regrease ahead of failure, which is a legitimate maintenance-planning signal.

population_detail.description: Same-vintage tracker rows in Red Clay Flats blocks B04, B05 and zone Z that the narratives say are 'all coming up to that age together'.
population_detail.basis: not quantifiable from this data - no installed base, row count or vintage roster was provided; only 7 serviced assets are named.

hypotheses.statement: Red Clay Flats contains a single-vintage cohort of tracker drives (blocks B04, B05 and zone Z) whose factory grease is reaching end of service life simultaneously, so the site rate is an age-cohort effect rather than a defect.
predictions: All 7 asset_ids fall into a small number of blocks/zones (B04, B05, Z) rather than being spread uniformly across the site's tracker population.
Other sites in the fleet with the same commissioning vintage/tracker model show elevated drive_grease_degradation rates once normalised by GW-months; younger sites show near-zero.
The per-event severity stays low: labor_hours ~2-7h, lost_mwh_reported = 0, resolution codes dominated by CLEANED/ADJUSTED rather than structural failures.
Event dates should keep accumulating at a roughly steady or slowly rising rate across 2024-2026 rather than spiking once and stopping.
Narratives should repeatedly reference age/vintage ('same vintage', 'due for it') and rarely reference an external trigger.
discriminating_evidence: Cross-tab site rate against drive age/vintage: if age explains the lift, same-vintage assets at other sites match Red Clay Flats' rate and the site term collapses.
If assets at Red Clay Flats of DIFFERENT vintages also show the symptom at elevated rate, age-cohort is falsified and a site-local cause is implied.
Recurrence flags: true end-of-life wear should show few repeat WOs on the same asset_id within 12 months after regrease; a site-local driver would show repeats.

hypotheses.statement: A site-local condition at Red Clay Flats (abrasive clay dust ingress past drive seals, or a wrong/incompatible grease spec used at this site) is accelerating grease breakdown, producing genuine ~10x lift over the fleet independent of asset age.
predictions: Narrative text at this site should mention contamination descriptors ('gritty', 'dried out', 'separated', dust/soil) at higher frequency than the same symptom elsewhere in the fleet.
Repeat WOs on the same asset_id at shortening intervals after a regrease (grease degrading faster than the design interval).
Other dust/seal-sensitive symptoms at Red Clay Flats (bearing wear, slew drive backlash, motor current alarms) should also be elevated versus fleet, not just grease.
The symptom should appear across multiple vintages/blocks at the site, including any newer rows.
Parts consumption of grease cartridges / gearboxes per GW-month at this site should exceed fleet median.
discriminating_evidence: Time-to-recurrence on regreased assets: short recurrence intervals support H2; long or absent recurrence supports H1.
Presence of the symptom on the site's newest tracker rows would separate H2 from the vintage-cohort story.
Whether the elevation is confined to the grease symptom only (argues H1/artifact) or spans several tribology-related symptoms at the site (argues H2).

hypotheses.statement: The cluster is a coding/reporting artifact: routine grease servicing that is captured as PM (or not captured at all) elsewhere in the fleet is being written up as corrective work orders at Red Clay Flats by a handful of technicians, inflating the CM-based rate without any real difference in drive condition.
predictions: All or nearly all 7 WOs are wo_type = CM with zero lost_mwh_reported and low priority (P2/P3), i.e. no production impact recorded.

The 7 WOs concentrate on very few techs (TECH-0215, TECH-0063, TECH-0173 account for all of them here); fleet-wide, those tech IDs should show above-average use of the grease symptom wherever they work.

Sites with low drive_grease_degradation CM rates should show correspondingly high PM work-order counts on tracker_drive lubrication tasks, so combined PM+CM lubrication touches per GW-month are similar across sites.

Internal inconsistency in the records supports loose data entry: resolution_code disagreeing with extracted action (CLEANED vs part_replaced, PART-REPL vs cleaned_or_serviced) and parts fields listing 'gearbox x3/x4' on jobs described as a repack.
Near-verbatim duplicate narratives between WO-2026-00664 and WO-2026-00688 indicate template/copy-paste entry rather than independent observations.
discriminating_evidence: Add PM work orders to the denominator/numerator: if total lubrication touches per GW-month equalise across sites, the site lift is an artifact.
Tech-level rate comparison: if the same techs show elevated grease-symptom coding at other sites they cover, the effect travels with the tech, not the site.
Text-similarity check across the 7 narratives; high duplication implies fewer independent events than n=7 suggests.

hypotheses.statement: With only 7 events on 2.9 GW-months, the apparent 10x lift is small-number noise amplified by batched inspection visits — the events arrive in same-week pairs because a tech sweeping a block writes several WOs at once, so effective independent events are ~4, not 7.
predictions: Event dates cluster into tight pairs/triples (2024-07-26/29; 2025-12-06/22; 2026-06-24/28) with long empty gaps, rather than being Poisson-spread over 24+ months.
Within each date pair the tech and block are the same or adjacent, consistent with one dispatch generating multiple WOs.
Other small-exposure sites in the fleet should show comparable or larger lifts on some symptom purely by chance; a fleet-wide scan of site-symptom lifts should contain several 5-10x outliers at n<10.
A Poisson/negative-binomial confidence interval on 7 events over 2.9 GW-months should be wide and, after clustering correction, may overlap plausible fleet variation.
No trend in event rate over time once batched visits are collapsed to single dispatch events.
discriminating_evidence: Collapse same-week, same-tech WOs into one dispatch event and recompute rate and significance; if the lift falls below the fleet's outlier threshold, H4 is favoured over H1/H2.
Compare against the distribution of lifts for all site-symptom pairs with n<10; if this candidate sits inside that null distribution, it is ordinary variation.
Continued accrual of new grease WOs at Red Clay Flats after 2026-06 at >1 per 2 months would falsify H4 and support a real site effect.
